subtitle: Crypto-equity correlation isn't constant. Sometimes it's near +1 (everything moves together), sometimes near 0 (crypto trades on its own narrative). The regime determines whether macro signals override crypto-specific setups. Read the regime; adjust accordingly.

blocks.content:
You've learned the macro stack (DXY, VIX, ES) and how it affects crypto. But that influence isn't constant. Sometimes crypto is glued to equities — every NASDAQ move shows up in BTC. Other times crypto trades on its own narrative — BTC rallies despite tech weakness because of an ETF approval, or crashes alone after a major exchange failure.

Knowing which CORRELATION REGIME you're in tells you whether to lean on macro signals or trade crypto-specific setups primarily.

Correlation between BTC and equities (typically S&P 500 or NASDAQ) is measured statistically over rolling time windows. Range: -1 to +1.

  • +1.0: BTC and equities move in perfect sync
  • +0.5 to +1.0: high correlation — they generally move together
  • 0 to +0.5: weak correlation — sometimes together, sometimes not
  • 0: no correlation — independent moves
  • -0.5 to 0: weak inverse correlation
  • -1.0: perfect inverse (extremely rare)

Most charting platforms can plot rolling correlation. Periods like 30-day or 60-day BTC-vs-NASDAQ correlation tell you the current regime.

rows: Crypto moves with equities. Macro signals (DXY, VIX, ES) dominate. Trade crypto WITH macro bias; counter-macro setups have low win rate.
Crypto partially independent. Trade crypto setups normally; macro is a soft factor.
Crypto on its own. Macro signals matter little; crypto-specific narratives dominate. Trade individual setups primarily.

blocks.content:
Correlation regimes change for predictable reasons:

  • Macro stress events: high correlation spikes during risk events. Everything moves together when fear is dominant.
  • Crypto-specific catalysts: ETF approval, major regulatory news, exchange failure, halving. These temporarily decouple crypto from broader risk markets.
  • Bull/bear market phases: crypto often decouples DURING raging bull markets (retail crypto FOMO ignores equity weakness) and re-couples DURING bear markets (everything sells together).
  • Liquidity conditions: tight global liquidity = high correlation; abundant liquidity = lower correlation.
  • Long-term trends: BTC's correlation with equities has been gradually rising as institutional adoption grows (institutions trade BTC similarly to other risk assets).

blocks.title: Crypto is becoming MORE correlated over time
blocks.content:
Historically (pre-2020), BTC was largely independent of equities. Post-2020, the correlation has trended higher — especially post-2022 ETF approvals brought institutional flows. The 'digital gold' narrative (BTC as inverse-equity hedge) has weakened.

Implication: macro signals matter MORE for crypto trading today than they did 5 years ago. The trader who ignores DXY/VIX/ES is operating with outdated mental models. Macro awareness is increasingly essential.

rows: Lead with macro analysis. If macro risk-on, look for crypto longs. If macro risk-off, look for crypto shorts or sit out. Crypto-only setups against macro often fail.
Balanced. Crypto setups are primary; macro is supplementary context. Reduce conviction when crypto setup conflicts with macro direction.
Crypto narratives dominate. Focus on crypto-specific signals (BTC dominance, ETF news, on-chain metrics). Macro is background.

blocks.content: How to spot regime SHIFTS in real time

Regime shifts often happen visibly. Watch for:

  • Major catalyst: BTC ETF approval, major exchange failure, banking crisis, etc. These often trigger regime shifts immediately.
  • Correlation breaking: BTC rallies 5% on a day when NASDAQ is flat or down. The decoupling itself is the signal.
  • Sentiment shift: F&G changes dramatically due to crypto-specific news without equity sentiment shifting similarly.
  • BTC.D moves independent of equity moves: capital flowing within crypto regardless of broader risk environment.

Recognizing the regime shift early lets you adjust strategy before the new dynamics fully play out.

Example 1 — HIGH correlation regime: VIX has spiked to 32 over the last 2 weeks. BTC and NASDAQ correlation rising to +0.85. NASDAQ fell 4% today. BTC is down 5% in the same window. Bearish equity environment dominating.

Approach: assume macro signals lead crypto. Don't try to long BTC despite individual setup quality. Wait for VIX to normalize and correlation to ease before resuming crypto-specific setups. Even strong crypto charts often fail when macro is pulling everything down.

Example 2 — DECOUPLED regime: Spot BTC ETF was just approved (major positive crypto catalyst). BTC rallied 10% on the news while NASDAQ was flat. 30-day correlation has dropped from +0.7 to +0.2 over the past week.

Approach: trade crypto-specific setups primarily. The ETF narrative is driving BTC; macro signals matter less. Position based on BTC's chart, BTC.D, ETF flow data. Macro is background context but not the primary driver.

blocks.title: Don't assume regime persistence
blocks.content:
Regimes change. A decoupled phase eventually re-couples. A high-correlation period eventually relaxes. Don't assume the current regime will continue indefinitely.

Practical: re-evaluate the regime monthly. Check rolling correlation. Note major catalysts that might shift dynamics. Adjust your macro-vs-technical weighting accordingly.

blocks.title: Take this with you
blocks.content:
Three rules:

  1. Identify the current correlation regime. 30/60-day BTC-vs-NASDAQ correlation tells you whether macro signals dominate or crypto narratives do.
  2. Adjust trading approach by regime. High correlation = lead with macro. Decoupled = crypto-specific signals primary. Mixed = both factors.
  3. Watch for regime SHIFTS. Major catalysts and breaking correlations signal new dynamics. Adjust before the regime fully plays out.

You've now completed Tier 5. The Tier 5 Final tests macro and context integration. Then Tier 6 (Execution & Journaling) completes the curriculum.
